scope: Proposition 7.3 (Convergence of stopped carpets) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The wired boundary cluster converges jointly with hδ, with its labels, to A−a,a(h). In a free flat parent, after subtracting its label and writing f for the zero-boundary limiting remainder, the first odd carpet converges to A−2a,2a(f). At depth r, define the global closed carpet as the closed complement of the holes still unsearched after every branch has met r odd rims; it includes all earlier layers and, in the wired case, the first wired layer. For each fixed finite r, this global carpet converges in ordinary Hausdorff distance to the corresponding canonical nested carpet. Its labels and restarted zero-boundary fields converge on every finite family of pointed compact buffers in the limiting holes. These pointed conclusions include distinct limiting components with the same discrete precursor; they do not assign one whole precursor carpet to several separate Hausdorff limits.
